scenes.heading: How a Python loop works
scenes.narration: Welcome! Today we will learn how a Python loop works. A loop lets your program repeat a task again and again, without writing the same code many times.

scenes.heading: The for loop
scenes.narration: Here is a simple for loop. The range(3) call gives us the numbers 0, 1 and 2. For each number, the variable i takes that value, and print shows it on the screen.

scenes.heading: How the loop runs
scenes.narration: Watch how the loop runs. First, i is 0, and print shows 0. Then i becomes 1, then 2, and after that the loop stops.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.subheading: A loop repeats code for every value
scenes.narration: To recap, a loop repeats the same code for every value. Use range to say how many times, and print to see each result. Now try changing the number inside range yourself!

quiz.question: What numbers does range(3) give the loop?
quiz.explanation: range(3) starts at 0 and stops before 3, so it gives 0, 1 and 2.

quiz.question: What does print(i) do inside the loop?
options: Shows the value of i on the screen
quiz.explanation: Each time the loop runs, print shows the current value of i on the screen.

quiz.question: Why do we use a loop?
options: To make the computer run faster
To write the same code many times
To repeat a task without writing the same code again
To sort a list of numbers
quiz.explanation: A loop repeats the same code for every value, so you only write it once.
